sources.title: OWASP JSON Web Token Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened JWT structure and trust guidance. Signed claims are not automatically application authority; verify actual token library configuration.

sources.title: OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened cookie, session lifecycle, renewal, and expiration guidance. Rolling reference, not a browser/runtime compatibility baseline.

sources.title: RFC 8725: JSON Web Token Best Current Practices
sources.notes: Opened RFC Editor presentation of algorithm, issuer, audience, explicit typing, and cross-JWT confusion guidance. Original RFC URL redirected to this direct RFC page.

sources.title: RFC 9700: Best Current Practice for OAuth 2.0 Security
sources.notes: Opened OAuth security BCP including audience restriction and replay considerations. Apply requirements to the actual OAuth role/flow; no universal provider implementation claim.

sources.title: OWASP Forgot Password Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened recovery request, token generation, single-use/expiry, and enumeration guidance. Does not establish any project's recovery implementation.

sources.title: OWASP Authorization Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened authentication/authorization distinction and contextual enforcement guidance. Public access can be intentional; no missing-annotation verdict rule.

sources.title: OWASP Authorization Patterns Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened service/gateway placement, PEP/PDP/PAP/PIP responsibilities, context propagation, and failure behavior. Local policies are not inherently fail-open.

sources.title: OWASP Authorization Decisions And Output Handling Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened decision binding, batch correlation, authorized collections, and constraint enforcement guidance. Collection semantics must be established rather than universally all-or-deny.

sources.title: OWASP Authorization Policy And Data Distribution Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened authoritative attributes, ownership/freshness requirements, replication, publication versus activation, and outage considerations. No universal cache TTL is prescribed.

sources.title: OWASP Multi Tenant Security Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened verified membership/context propagation and tenant isolation guidance. Query parameterization and supplied tenant IDs are not proof of membership.

sources.title: Spring Security: Method Security
sources.notes: Opened method-security activation, invocation advice, result authorization, and request/method distinction. Rolling documentation; verify target Spring version and effective proxy/advice call path.

sources.title: Quarkus: Authorization of Web Endpoints
sources.notes: Opened endpoint policy matching and annotation/configuration interaction. Rolling guide, not evidence of fixture qualification or behavior across all Quarkus versions.

sources.title: Micronaut Security Guide
sources.notes: Opened security filter/principal and intercept URL map sections. Latest guide is mutable; inspect installed version, rule ordering, and enabled configuration before conclusions.

sources.title: Jakarta Security 3.0 Specification
sources.notes: Opened HttpAuthenticationMechanism/container invocation and caller establishment. This is a 3.0 reference, not a claim that every Jakarta deployment implements that revision.

sources.title: Express: Using Middleware
sources.notes: Opened application/router middleware registration, mount paths, and next/end behavior. Effective registration/call order must be inspected in the target application.

sources.title: NestJS: Guards
sources.notes: Opened canActivate and execution context guidance. Guard presence alone does not establish transport adaptation, binding, or object authorization.

sources.title: Fastify: Hooks
sources.notes: Opened request/reply hook ordering, registration, and encapsulation scope. Latest docs are mutable; no cross-version plugin behavior is assumed.

sources.title: Koa Documentation
sources.notes: Opened cascading middleware, app composition, and proxy settings. Trace before/after next and the actual listener/proxy topology.

sources.title: OWASP Mass Assignment Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened binding threat and language/framework solution sections. Distinguish effective JSON deserialization, form binders, explicit mappings, and server-owned fields.

sources.title: OWASP GraphQL Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened resolver, schema, authorization, batching, and DoS considerations. Recipes use semantic schemas and actual sink controls, not a universal alphanumeric input restriction.

sources.title: OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened binding, structural token mapping, escaping limitations, and least privilege. Safe value binding does not establish object authorization.

sources.title: OWASP NoSQL Security Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened query-object/operator injection and driver/ODM guidance. Confirm exact driver and query semantics; generic JSON parsing is not a sanitizer.

sources.title: OWASP LDAP Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened distinguished-name versus search-filter encoding and structured framework defenses. SQL or HTML escaping must not be substituted.

sources.title: OWASP XPath Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened fixed expressions, variable binding, Java resolver pattern, and application-owned query structure. Compiling concatenated expressions does not bind values.

sources.title: OWASP OS Command Injection Defense Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened command versus argument injection and avoidance/parameterization guidance. Argument-array invocation does not eliminate program option semantics.

sources.title: Node.js: Child Process
sources.notes: Opened exec shell behavior and process options. Rolling runtime docs; inspect actual Node version, executable, platform, and explicit shell settings.

sources.title: Java SE 21: ProcessBuilder
sources.notes: Opened command-list, environment, directory, and process-attribute semantics. Reference is Java SE 21; platform/executable argument parsing still matters.

sources.title: OWASP Server-Side Template Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened template-source, second-pass evaluation, template selection, and context guidance. Distinguish server evaluation from browser output escaping.

sources.title: Spring Framework: Expression Evaluation
sources.notes: Opened expression parsing, constructors, root objects, and evaluation context examples. No claim that every context exposes the same capabilities.

sources.title: Node.js: VM
sources.notes: Opened the explicit warning that VM contexts are not a security mechanism for untrusted code. No sandbox escape payload or version-specific exploit claim is included.

sources.title: OWASP SSRF Prevention Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened fixed-trusted versus broad-external destination cases and application/network controls. Actual redirects, resolution, connection, and credentials require target-specific tracing.

sources.title: OWASP Cross Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened framework escape hatches, context-specific encoding, and HTML sanitization. Recipes do not assume browser/framework behavior from an API name alone.

sources.title: OWASP DOM Based XSS Prevention Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened DOM source/context distinction and nested parser contexts. Follow later decoding/mutation rather than treating encoding as context-independent.

sources.title: React: Dangerously Setting the Inner HTML
sources.notes: Opened raw HTML, Trusted Types policy responsibility, and Markdown preview discussion. Rolling docs; no blanket React version guarantee or universal execution claim.

sources.title: OWASP Cross-Site Request Forgery Prevention Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened browser credential model, framework/token mechanisms, origin/Fetch Metadata, and SameSite caveats. Evaluate actual ambient credentials and effective alternative defenses.

sources.title: OWASP HTML5 Security Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened web messaging, exact origin validation, targetOrigin, CORS, and frame guidance. Messages remain data even from a permitted origin.

sources.title: MDN: Window.postMessage
sources.notes: Opened security concerns and origin/source/targetOrigin examples. API documentation supplements OWASP; target browser and opaque-origin handling need actual validation.

sources.title: MDN: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing
sources.notes: Opened credentialed requests and response readability examples. Distinguish sent request effects, browser reads, preflight, and server authorization.

sources.title: OWASP Unvalidated Redirects And Forwards Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened fixed versus caller-supplied destinations and internal-forward authorization considerations. Establish concrete phishing/disclosure/bypass impact separately.

sources.title: OWASP File Upload Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened content/filename/storage threats, expanded-size risk, and layered upload defenses. No automatic malware-service execution or external file submission is authorized.

sources.title: Java SE 21: Path
sources.notes: Opened resolve, normalize, and filesystem/symlink caveats. Lexical normalization is not a realpath containment or race guarantee.

sources.title: Node.js: File System
sources.notes: Opened access/exists-before-open race warnings and filesystem APIs. Actual filesystem, platform flags, and attacker control determine containment conclusions.

sources.title: Amazon S3: Download And Upload Objects With Presigned URLs
sources.notes: Opened bearer capability, signer permissions, temporary-credential expiry, and request-time expiration behavior. S3-specific; do not generalize lifetime/revocation to other providers.

sources.title: OWASP Deserialization Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened native object construction and Java/data-format guidance. Format presence is not proof of a reachable gadget or remote code execution.

sources.title: Java SE 21: Serialization Filtering
sources.notes: Opened Oracle filtering overview and linked filter topics. Verify effective stream/filter configuration and matching JDK before implementation-specific conclusions.

sources.title: OWASP XML External Entity Prevention Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened DTD/entities, XInclude, schema/stylesheet external access, resource limits, and unsupported-setting handling. Parser/provider defaults are version-specific.

sources.title: Java SE 21: JAXP Security Guide
sources.notes: Opened external resource mechanisms and entity expansion discussion. Reference is JDK 21; no universal XML factory hardening snippet is claimed.

sources.title: yaml Package Documentation
sources.notes: Opened parser/document options, schema and conversion API structure. Applies to this library, not all Node YAML loaders or Java YAML implementations.

sources.title: OWASP Prototype Pollution Prevention Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened maps/null-prototype objects and freeze/seal limitations. A suspicious own JSON key is not by itself mutation of a shared prototype.

sources.title: OWASP Secrets Management Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened lifecycle, CI, delivery, auditing, and incident-response structure. No source candidate was validated against a provider; no secret-scanner version/maintenance claim is made.

sources.title: OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened adaptive hashes, salt/pepper, work factors, legacy migration, and input limits. Numeric policy is deliberately not frozen into the card; check current source and installed library.

sources.title: OWASP Cryptographic Storage Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened threat-model/encryption-layer distinctions, primitive/mode, randomness, and key lifecycle guidance. Does not certify protocols or imply field encryption is always required.

sources.title: Node.js: Crypto
sources.notes: Opened crypto API structure and randomBytes cryptographic randomness definition. Match comparison, nonce, and algorithm behavior to the actual runtime/library.

sources.title: OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened event provenance, purpose, fields, and data-exclusion discussion. Redacted evidence and useful authorized diagnostics are compatible; no live log store was inspected.

sources.title: OWASP Error Handling Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened exception/stack exposure and framework error-handling discussion. Severity depends on actual disclosed information and audience, not a stack-trace keyword.

sources.title: OWASP User Privacy Protection Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened privacy/anonymity threat framing. Used as privacy context, not current legal advice, a retention mandate, or a substitute for the password/TLS-specific sources.

sources.title: OWASP GitHub Actions Security Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened privileged workflow, credential, cache, and untrusted-code considerations. Suggested scanning/automation in the source does not authorize enabling it during review.

sources.title: GitHub Actions: Secure Use Reference
sources.notes: Opened untrusted checkout triggers, shell interpolation, permissions, actions, and artifact/cache risks. Redirected from the older hardening URL; no action-version feature guarantee is embedded.

sources.title: OSV-Scanner Documentation
sources.notes: Opened official dependency-to-advisory purpose and documentation entrypoint. Installed version, supported inputs, advisory freshness, offline/network behavior, and flags must be checked before any use.

sources.title: Semgrep: Taint Analysis Overview
sources.notes: Opened source/sink/sanitizer rule semantics and modeling options. No engine/edition cross-file capability or framework completeness is assumed.

sources.title: GitHub: Code Scanning With CodeQL
sources.notes: Opened language/framework model limitations and query-pack discussion. No autobuild, hosted scanning enablement, licensing entitlement, or target coverage is implied.

sources.title: OWASP Docker Security Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened daemon/socket authority, runtime user, capabilities, and isolation guidance. A read-only socket mount does not itself restrict Docker API operations.

sources.title: Kubernetes: Pod Security Standards
sources.notes: Opened profile distinctions, host namespaces/mounts, non-root controls, policy instantiation, and OS/version caveats. A standard is not evidence that admission enforcement is active.

sources.title: OWASP Infrastructure As Code Security Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened configuration/monitoring and provisioning security context. Generic guidance does not qualify every IaC language/provider or authorize plan/apply execution.

sources.title: OWASP Transport Layer Security Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened TLS security properties, certificate/hostname, and traffic-leg guidance. Actual termination topology and client trust configuration remain application-specific.

sources.title: OWASP Business Logic Security Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened server-owned values, explicit workflows, concurrency, and idempotency topics. Product invariants determine required approvals and allowed automatic effects.

sources.title: OWASP Webhook Security Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened authenticity, replay, duplicate, and publisher-side threats. Cards defer to actual provider algorithms/fields rather than universalizing the summary's HMAC/timestamp examples.

sources.title: Stripe: Webhooks
sources.notes: Opened endpoint verification and raw-body requirements. Match installed SDK and event mechanism; no live Stripe events, account, or signing secret were used.

sources.title: GitHub: Validating Webhook Deliveries
sources.notes: Opened X-Hub-Signature-256, payload HMAC, encoding, and constant-time comparison guidance. Do not assume a Stripe-like signed timestamp or that every delivery header is authenticated.

sources.title: OWASP Denial Of Service Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened resource/attack-surface methodology and layered controls. No load tests, measured capacity, or production availability claims follow from this reference.

sources.title: Node.js: Don't Block The Event Loop Or Worker Pool
sources.notes: Opened event-loop/worker-pool model and blocking/algorithmic-work topics. Documentation is Linux-centric where noted; investigate actual input bounds and runtime behavior.

sources.title: OWASP LLM Prompt Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened direct/indirect instruction carriers and tool/data impact framing. Recipes require a real authority/confidentiality/execution failure, not keyword matches or universal rejection of imperfect output.

sources.title: OWASP AI Agent Security Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened least-privilege tool scope, execution-side authorization, approval binding, and resource threats. No mandatory human approval for every write is inferred.

sources.title: OWASP RAG Security Cheat Sheet
sources.notes: Opened access-control inheritance, retrieval-time authorization, context/caches, and tool topics. No compliance or measured detection claim is adopted from the source.

sources.title: MCP: Security Best Practices, 2025-11-25 Documentation
sources.notes: Opened confused-deputy, token-passthrough, session, and discovery SSRF guidance. Older 2025-06-18 URL redirected here; this does not establish a target server's negotiated protocol or SDK capabilities.
